title: Adhar Configuration Schema
description: Schema for config.yaml matching current file structure

dnsProvider.description: Edge DNS backend for external-dns records and cert-manager DNS-01 wildcard certificates. Empty = the environment's cloud provider DNS; 'none' disables edge DNS (self-signed TLS); 'cloudflare' for on-prem/custom clusters (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN).

providers.description: Provider configurations keyed by provider name (e.g., civo, aws, azure)

environments.description: Environment definitions keyed by environment name (e.g., dev, test, staging, production)

keyValue.description: Key/value entry. Sizing keys (matched ignoring case and separators): controlPlaneMachineType - the control-plane size (compute mode); machineType | nodeSize | workerMachineType - the primary worker group's size; nodeCount - starting workers (whole number >= 0; 0 or absent = the provider default, 2 on every cloud); diskSizeGb - OS disk GiB (> 0; AWS and GCP - Azure reads providers.azure.config.diskSizeGb only); diskType - OS disk type; kubeVersion - Kubernetes version; podCidr - pod network CIDR.

helmChartConfig.description: Configuration for deploying a Helm chart

nodeGroups.description: Additional node groups (GPU, high-memory, ...). An environment's list replaces its template's.

isolation.description: What the environment physically is: a namespace on the shared platform cluster (default), or a dedicated cluster with its own platform install.

nodeGroups.description: Additional node groups (GPU, high-memory, ...). An environment's list replaces its template's.

provider.description: Name of the providers.<name> block this environment uses (default: the primary provider)

region.description: Region override for this environment (default: the provider's region). Checked against the provider's region-name format.

autoscalingConfig.description: Node autoscaling: the cluster is created with the configured worker count and the adhar-controlplane node autoscaler moves it between minWorkers and maxWorkers on demand

enabled.description: Enable the node autoscaler for this environment

minWorkers.description: Never scale below this many workers; must not exceed maxWorkers

maxWorkers.description: Never scale above this many workers (the spend ceiling); must be > 0 when enabled

nodeGroup.description: Node group to scale: `workers` (default) or the name of an entry in nodeGroups

scaleDownUtilizationThreshold.description: Requested-vs-allocatable share (e.g. "50%") that cluster CPU and memory must both stay under before a worker is removed

scaleDownDelay.description: How long the cluster must stay under the threshold before a worker is drained and removed (Go duration)

scaleUpCooldown.description: Minimum gap between two node additions (Go duration)

region.description: Region the cluster is built in. Format checked per provider: aws ap-southeast-1, gcp asia-southeast1 (a region, not a zone), azure centralindia, digitalocean blr1, civo LON1. Not required in clusterMode: provided.

clusterMode.description: Where the cluster comes from: compute (the default, kubeadm on raw instances this platform creates), managed (this cloud's hosted Kubernetes - EKS, AKS, GKE, DOKS, Civo k3s, created and owned by the platform) or provided (the cluster ALREADY EXISTS; the platform only installs itself onto it through the kubeconfig below, creates no infrastructure, and never deletes the cluster - adhar down leaves it running). The same three values for every provider; the service name is implied by the provider. The removed useManagedK8s boolean and the per-cloud spellings (eks/aks/gke/doks/k3s) are rejected rather than mapped, so a stale config fails loudly instead of quietly building the other mode.

kubeconfig.description: clusterMode: provided only - path to the kubeconfig that reaches the existing cluster. Defaults to $KUBECONFIG and then ~/.kube/config. Ignored in the other modes, where the platform writes its own kubeconfig.

kubeContext.description: clusterMode: provided only - the context inside that kubeconfig to install onto. Defaults to the file's current context. It is reduced to this one context before anything uses it, so the rest of your kubeconfig is never carried into the platform.

config.description: Provider-specific configuration. Shape varies per provider.

size.description: Civo legacy single size: sizes every node that controlPlaneMachineType/workerMachineType and the environment do not.

controlPlaneMachineType.description: Control-plane machine type (compute mode). Overridden by an environment's clusterConfig controlPlaneMachineType. Default: aws m6i.xlarge, azure Standard_D4s_v5, gcp e2-standard-4, digitalocean s-8vcpu-16gb, civo g3.large - each >= 4 vCPU / 16 GiB, because a 2-vCPU control plane collapses under the platform's ~600 CRDs.

workerMachineType.description: Default worker machine type for every node group that names none (and for scale-ups of an empty group). Overridden by clusterConfig machineType/nodeSize and nodeGroups[].machineType. Default: aws r6i.xlarge, azure Standard_E4bds_v5, gcp e2-standard-4, digitalocean s-8vcpu-16gb, civo g3.xlarge (compute) / g4s.kube.large (managed).

vpcConfig.description: AWS network: cidr (default 10.0.0.0/16), subnetCidrs [public - every node, private - internal load balancers] (default 10.0.1.0/24, 10.0.2.0/24), availabilityZones [public, private] (default: the region's first two; every node lands in the first).

nodeGroup.description: An ADDITIONAL node group beside the primary `workers` group (which clusterConfig machineType/nodeCount and the autoscaling block describe) - e.g. a GPU or high-memory pool. Created by every provider in both compute and managed mode; OS disk, image and network are the provider's. Labels and taints are applied by managed node pools; in compute mode they are recorded but kubeadm joins do not apply them yet.

name.description: DNS-1123 label, at most 20 characters; becomes part of every VM name. `workers` is the primary group and cannot be redefined here.

machineType.description: Machine type (AWS instance type, Azure VM size, GCP machine type, DigitalOcean droplet slug, Civo size). Empty = the provider's worker size (providers.<name>.config.workerMachineType, else the built-in default).
